transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-12 — 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Luis (Redwood SE), Jordan (CSM) — Priya (Nyx Head MLOps), Ethan (Platform), Sara (FP&A), Omar (SRE)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in. Quick agenda: we wanted to walk through the recent spike you saw last month, go over cost levers, reliability playbook for surges, and align on next steps for the roadmap and pilot. Is that good on your side Priya?

[00:14] Priya (Nyx): Yeah that works. We also want to get clarity on dedicated pool sizing and what fallback behavior looks like — like when your hosted rate limits kick in what happens. And, um, Sara wants some numbers for finance.

[00:28] Sara (Nyx - FP&A): Yep, budget owners are asking — if usage triples again how do we keep it from blowing the quarter.

[00:35] Luis (Redwood SE): Great — we'll cover modeling. Quick note: some terminology might be slightly off in the transcript, sorry if names get munged.

[00:45] Ethan (Nyx): No worries.

[01:02] Maya: Quick recap of the spike: Nyx had a 3x peak for 48 hours tied to a marketing campaign. You were on our hosted endpoint with a mix of chat & generation calls. Observed token mix shifted heavy tail with a lot of long outputs which drove token cost up.

[01:28] Omar (Nyx SRE): Correct — latency was fine mostly, but we saw queueing and a handful of 503s around the peak window. We want to avoid that next time.

[01:42] Luis: For the 503s it's typically a capacity vs concurrency issue — either the model reached its per-instance concurrency or internal queue overflowed. We can do two things: short term, enable burst capacity and adjust autoscaling thresholds; medium term, move part of your high-throughput workload to a Dedicated pool with reserved slots.

[02:04] Priya: Can you quantify expected unit cost delta between hosted with aggressive batching and the dedicated option? We need a quick spreadsheet example.

[02:16] Maya: Absolutely. We'll produce a table that compares current hosted spend vs dedicated with three configurations: baseline reserved, reserved + higher batch sizes, reserved + int8 quant profile. That'll show both token $/k and projected monthly spend under traffic curves.

[02:39] Sara: For finance it's key to see worst-case and expected-case. Also, we need to understand implications for SLA and data isolation since some of this workload touches PHI-ish info.

[02:52] Jordan (CSM): Noted — we'll include the isolation delta (hosted vs dedicated) and whether private deployment is required for PHI.

[03:10] Luis: On the technical levers — batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization matter most. For your type of prompts (many small prompts with occasional long threads) prefix caching yields big wins: cache the first 2-3 turns and avoid recompute. But cache hit rates depend on prompt variability.

[03:32] Priya: Our team has lots of parameterized prompts so hit rate might be moderate, say 30–40%. Worth it?

[03:40] Luis: Yes at that hit rate you still see meaningful token savings, particularly on the decode side. Also, intelligent batching: group short requests and auto-batch up to a 128-token effective length window — that reduces per-token amortized cost.

[04:00] Ethan: What's the expected latency impact when batching aggressively? Some of our UX is latency-sensitive.

[04:07] Luis: Tradeoff — more batching usually increases tail latency if you wait too long for batch fill. But Redwood supports adaptive batching: we cap wait window so latency SLOs are preserved while getting batching benefits for high throughput paths. We'll show recommended batch windows by route in the spreadsheet.

[04:26] Sara: Okay good. From finance perspective we also want to model quantization risk — if int8/4 changes output quality we need to see fallback policies.

[04:37] Maya: We'll include a quality delta note. Luis, can you summarize how quant profiles and rollouts typically work?

[04:44] Luis: Sure. You can deploy a quantized variant and route a small percentage (canary) of traffic. Redwood's rollout supports A/B and automatic fallback if evals detect regressions. For critical paths we suggest 5–10% canary with targeted eval prompts (your top 15). If output quality dips beyond threshold we automatically roll back.

[05:03] Priya: That rollback automation is important. Also — can we pin model versions across environments? We need reproducible inference for audit.

[05:10] Maya: Yes — pinning and model versioning is supported. We'll capture that in the security pack.

[05:22] Omar: On the reliability side — what about multi-region fallback? If region A is overloaded can traffic route to B automatically?

[05:30] Luis: Yes, smart routing can send requests by policy and do automatic fallback to a compatible variant/region. For your latency constraints we'll recommend primary region plus warm standby.

[05:43] Ethan: Any gotchas for private VPC deployment if we later go that route? Networking and KMS are the main things.

[05:50] Jordan: For Private we provide a customer-managed control plane and KMS/HSM integrations. There is an on-prem option but it adds operational overhead. We'll include a simple network diagram and a KMS integration checklist.

[06:10] Priya: We need SOC2 attestations and audit logs for some customers — do you provide per-request audit logs?

[06:17] Maya: Yes, we can provide audit logs; retention tiers are an add-on. We will include SOC2 scope and the audit log retention options in the pack.

[06:30] Sara: Back to numbers — what's a plausible cost reduction from batching + caching + int8 for our mix? Even high-level percentage.

[06:39] Luis: Ballpark: batching + prefix caching might reduce unit tokens by 20–30%, int8 another 10–20% depending on model. Combined, best-case around 35–45% on token cost for throughput-heavy workloads. We'll model pessimistic/optimistic cases.

[07:00] Maya: We'll send a spreadsheet with three scenarios: conservative, expected, aggressive, and show monthly run-rate under each.

[07:12] (short cross talk)

[07:22] Priya: For the benchmark you mentioned — what exactly will you run?

[07:28] Luis: We'll run a dedicated pool perf test: synthetic traffic shaped from your 7-day trace, with three profiles: normal, spike (3x), and sustained high (1.5x for a week). We'll capture p95/p99 latency, error rates, and cost per million tokens. We'll also instrument KV cache hit rate.

[07:48] Ethan: Sounds good. We'll share the trace.

[08:00] Omar: For SRE, we want playbooks for surge — thresholds, when to scale, when to spill to dedicated, and how to notify.

[08:09] Jordan: We'll draft a surge playbook with thresholds (CPU/GPU util, queue depth), recommended autoscale params, and notification runbook.

[08:20] Priya: One more thing: compliance around data residency — a few customers require EU-only processing. Do you support region pinning?

[08:29] Maya: Yes region pinning and routing by legal domain are supported in Private or Dedicated; hosted can restrict regionally but for strict EU-only you'd likely choose Dedicated or Private. We'll note that in the pack.

[08:45] Sara: Great.

[08:52] Maya: Recap / next steps: 1) Maya to send cost scenarios spreadsheet + quality notes [due Aug 16]. 2) Priya to share 7-day traffic trace + top 15 prompts [due Aug 18]. 3) Luis to run dedicated perf benchmark (week of Aug 24) and share raw results [due Aug 21]. 4) Redwood to share SOC2 + SSO/SAML + KMS integration docs and a network diagram [due Aug 17]. 5) Schedule follow-up to review benchmark and decide on pilot (suggest Aug 27).

[09:28] Priya: That timeline works. One ask — please mark the benchmarking results as confidential for now; it's part of procurement.

[09:36] Maya: Absolutely. We'll flag the artifact.

[09:44] Ethan: Any risks we should call out?

[09:48] Luis: Quality regression with heavy quantization is the main one — mitigated via canary evals and rollback. Also, if your traffic is super unpredictable short-timescale bursts might still cause queueing unless we reserve capacity ahead of big campaigns.

[10:05] Sara: Finance note — if we move to Dedicated we need to align procurement timeline for reserved capacity commitments. We'll coordinate with Maya.

[10:15] Maya: Good point — we'll walk procurement options in a separate call if you want.

[10:21] (wrap-up)

[10:30] Priya: Thanks everyone — useful meeting. Looking forward to the spreadsheet and the benchmark.

[10:35] Maya: Thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark review.

[10:40] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript: occasional transcription errors (proper nouns and acronyms) may be present. References shared: Cost spreadsheet (to be attached), SOC2/security pack link (to be shared), benchmark logs (to be shared).
